issue.masthead: no. 160 · North Hollow · sunrise 07:21 · waxing crescent

pieces.title: On the first cold morning
pieces.body: "The first morning you can see your breath while pouring coffee is always the best day of September. You know the wood stove works, the apples are picked, and you do not have to mow the lawn again until May."

pieces.title: First heating cycle of the season completed
pieces.body: The hall thermostat called for heat at four forty-five this morning when interior hall temperatures dropped below sixty-three degrees. The oil burner ran for twenty-two minutes, sending hot water through the downstairs cast iron radiators without incident. By sunrise the main rooms were sixty-six degrees, and the system dropped back to idle as sunlight struck the parlour glass.

pieces.title: Winter squash harvest moves to porch racks
pieces.body: Thirty-four butternut squashes and eighteen delicatas were clipped from the vine yesterday afternoon before the cold front passed over. The stems were cut long and wiped with dry burlap, and the squash now rest in single layers across slatted wooden racks on the sunny back porch to harden their skins in the afternoon sun.

pieces.title: County tax inquiry window opens
pieces.body: The annual property tax assessment letter sits in the inbox, giving residents thirty days to review the revised building and woodlot valuation. Nora plans to compare the listed square footage against the tax maps on Tuesday before filing the paperwork in the attic deed box.
